rationale: Carendre is a proper geographical name (Carinthia/Carantania), denoting a distinct territorial/administrative region in early medieval Europe. The gloss "province" here refers to a concrete geographic and political territory — a constituent district — rather than a figurative "sphere of activity." The attestations in Orosius (Ors. 1, 1) further confirm a geographic/political sense, making state.n.01 (territory of an administrative district) the best fit over the abstract province.n.02.
